- [LGRA.2.9.6.4] **Timestamp** (`:%…`) — a pattern of directives and literal
  text, applied to a `Time`. The directives are Python's, and DS admits only
  these:

  | Directive | Renders |
  |---|---|
  | `%Y` | the year, four digits |
  | `%m` | the month, `01`–`12` |
  | `%d` | the day of the month, `01`–`31` |
  | `%H` | the hour, `00`–`23` |
  | `%M` | the minute, `00`–`59` |
  | `%S` | the second, `00`–`59` |
  | `%f` | the microsecond, six digits; the nanoseconds below it are truncated, never rounded |
  | `%z` | the UTC offset as `+HHMM` or `-HHMM`, then `SS` when the offset has seconds, then `.ffffff` when it has a fraction of a second |
  | `%%` | a literal `%` |

  Every field renders in the value's own UTC offset. Every other character is
  written as it is. The compiler must refuse any other `%` sequence, and a
  timestamp spec on a value that is not a `Time`, with
  `DS_VALIDATE_INTERP_BAD_FORMAT`. The compiler resolves the pattern into
  literal text and fields, and no pattern reaches the runtime.
